observations: Photo 0 and 1 show the same used engine from slightly different angles, sitting outdoors on wet/oily asphalt alongside other engines (looks like a yard of pulled units).
A barcode/sticker is visible on the cam cover in photo 0 and 1 but the printed code is too small/blurred to read.
Alternator, pulleys, hoses and sensors are attached; wiring looks intact but corroded/rusted brackets are visible near the right side mounting bracket (photo 0, 1).
Photo 2 shows the cylinder head with the valve/cam cover removed, exposing four spark-plug wells; no plugs or coils are seated in the holes.
No VIN plate, engine code stamp, dipstick, or fluid is visible in any photo.
No video or sound of the engine running; no compression test, no oil color shown.
Watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI UCHENNA' overlays all three photos, consistent with a marketplace listing, not fraud evidence by itself.

identity.kind: used Toyota 4-cylinder engine assembly, seller claims RAV4 (XA20) fitment

claims.claim: Complete engine for Toyota vehicles like SUVs and Crossovers
claims.evidence: Photo 2 shows the valve cover removed and all four spark-plug wells empty, which is not consistent with a sealed 'complete' long block as sold.
No engine code plate, casting number, or VIN cross-reference is legible in any photo; fitment claims for engines are tied to exact engine code, not model name alone.

risks.risk: Exact engine code/displacement cannot be confirmed, which determines both price tier and real compatibility.
risks.proof: Close-up, in-focus photo of the stamped engine code on the block and the legible sticker/barcode on the cam cover.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified generic used Toyota engine, lowest tier for the claimed model family

risks.risk: Valve cover is off and spark plugs/coils are missing or not shown reinstalled, raising doubt about completeness and whether internals (cam, valves) were exposed to the open yard environment.
risks.proof: Photo of the reassembled engine with valve cover and all ignition components in place, plus a photo of the intake/exhaust manifolds attached.

risks.risk: No proof the engine runs, has compression, or does not leak/smoke.
risks.proof: Video clip of the engine cranking/running on a test stand with audible idle, or a compression test reading shown on camera.

risks.risk: Visible rust/corrosion on mounting brackets and dirt/oil film suggest long outdoor storage or water exposure, which can affect internal condition (rust in cylinders, bearing corrosion).
risks.proof: Photo of the oil dipstick and oil color, and a photo inside the cylinder bores if the head is off.
risks.if_unproven: priced as weather-exposed stock, below clean pulled-engine price

risks.risk: Mileage/history of the donor vehicle is unknown, which matters for used engine pricing.
risks.proof: Photo of an odometer reading or import tag/auction sheet from the donor vehicle.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown mileage, worst-case high-mileage assumption

proof_requests: Clear, in-focus photo of the engine code stamped on the block (not just the blurred sticker).
Photo of the engine fully reassembled with valve cover, spark plugs/coils, and intake manifold in place.
Video of the engine running or being cranked, with audible sound.
Photo of the oil dipstick/oil color and any coolant residue.
Any import/auction sheet or odometer photo from the donor vehicle.
response.reason: Used engine pricing in this market hinges on the exact engine code and confirmed completeness/running state, and both are unreadable or contradicted here (cover off, plugs missing, code illegible), so even a worst-case price cannot be anchored to the right comparable set without a clearer code photo and reassembly/running proof.
